summary: Brick light station on a cliff at Grand Island's north tip near Munising, Lake Superior: lit 1856, tower rebuilt 1867, discontinued 1961, privately owned since 1972.

light.characteristic: fourth order, fixed white, varied by a white flash every ninety seconds (1899); one-and-a-half-second flash every fifteen seconds from 1926

structures.type: first tower and dwelling (type not stated in the sources read)
structures.note: Torn down in 1867 (LighthouseFriends); USLHS dates the station 1856.

structures.type: square brick tower on cut-stone foundation
structures.note: Nine-foot-square tower attached to west gable of a 1.5-storey brick dwelling (LighthouseFriends); 73 ft to centre of lantern (USLHS).
Keeper's quarters in USLHS record (1867, brick).

structures.type: cliff stairway and tramway to boathouse
structures.note: Ladders and steps built 1860 on the cliffs (LighthouseFriends); the stairway and tramway rebuilt 1885, 229 ft to the boathouse.

events.note: Congress appropriates $5,000 for a lighthouse on Grand Island (3 March 1853)
Fourth-order Fresnel lens; focal plane 204 ft above Lake Superior
Lighthouse Board finds the station 'in a wretched condition' from inferior materials in original construction
Congress provides $17,000 (23 July 1866) to rebuild the lighthouse
Old tower and dwelling torn down; new brick tower and dwelling built
Fourth-order lens fitted in the new tower's lantern
Late November gale tears away 43 ft of the cliff stairway (keeper's log as quoted by LighthouseFriends)
Board's list of lights gives: fourth order, fixed white, varied by a white flash every ninety seconds
Land no longer needed for light-house purposes sold at auction at Munising, 10 June 1901 (about 393 acres per LighthouseFriends)
Assistant keeper Edward S. Morrison found dead in a sailboat in June; keeper George Genry missing, body found 12 July 1908
Illuminant changed from oil to incandescent oil vapour
Changed on 4 October 1926 to a 1.5 s white flash every 15 s; station becomes unwatched
Original light discontinued; battery light on a twelve-foot post nearby
Station bought by a private owner, who restores the lighthouse and outbuildings
Cleveland-Cliffs sells the island to the Forest Service; Congress designates a national recreation area

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1867 date is the present brick tower and dwelling; the first light of 1856 was a wooden tower torn down in 1867 (LighthouseFriends). The record's 'first_lit 1856' is correct for the first light.
The station record's first lit date of 1856 is the first light, which LighthouseFriends and the USLHS record both date to that year; the 1867 tower is the present structure.

notes_for_editor: Moderate evidence, shorter than a rich station: the Light-House Board has only the 1899 list line and the 1901 land sale for this light in the local corpus; no Light-House Board narrative for Grand Island North was in the corpus, and the pre-1891 Board reports are not held. Most of the building and keeper detail rests on LighthouseFriends, which is copyrighted and cites logs and books; treat its passages as second-hand and check them against the station log or the National Archives before printing. (1) The 1866 rebuild money: LighthouseFriends says $17,000 on 23 July 1866; the USCG Historian's summary (not readable through the archive in my session) reportedly gives $12,000. Not resolved. (2) The first assistant in 1856: the USLHS roster says Edward Chambers; LighthouseFriends says Francis Chambers. (3) The 1941 automation date appears on a local history page (northernmichiganhistory.com, unsourced); LighthouseFriends gives 1926 (unwatched). The story gives 1926 and does not use 1941. (4) The focal height: the USLHS record gives 205 feet above water; LighthouseFriends gives 204 feet for the 1856 focal plane; the station record says 57.9 m. (5) The 1915 bulletin line says 'Grand Island, Lake Superior, Mich.' and does not say North; the Grand Island Harbor range lights are a different station. I identified the line as the north light by place; a reviewer should confirm. (6) The 1908 deaths: the Detroit Times spells the keeper 'Genery' and the assistant 'E. S. Morrison'; the roster spells 'Genry' and 'Edward S. Morrison'. The 1908 Life-Saving Service at Au Sable is named in the newspaper but not researched. The story does not name the owner or the family members, who are private; LighthouseFriends names the owner (a professor and author); the story does not name the owner. (7) The keepers' roster is the USLHS transcription (confirm each keeper in a primary record before naming in print); the 1908 keeper names rest on the newspapers. (8) NRHP 85002149: the nomination PDF is not digitised; the 1985 date in the station record was not checked. (9) The station record's 'Fl W 6s' and the record's 'Grand Island North' tower 22.2 m agree with the USLHS 73 ft; the characteristic does not match either the 1899 list or the 1926 change. (10) The story's footnote for LighthouseFriends is a single site cited for many facts; if the fact-checker wants page-level detail it has none. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the July 1908 Detroit Times items are read from OCR, which gives the assistant's initials as 'E. F.' in July and 'E. S.' in June (unresolved); the 1915 Bulletin line does not say which Grand Island light it means; LighthouseFriends' owner passage is not used; page images were not viewed.
